page.overview:
Who is Erendis?

Erendis, also known as The Mariner’s Wife, was the unhappy and later estranged wife of Tar-Aldarion, King of Númenor from SA 883 to SA 1075.

Erendis was born to Beregar and Núneth, who were descended from a minor branch of the Númenórean nobility descended from the House of Bëor. This was a lineage of lesser status than that of the royal house, entailing a shorter lifespan. She and her parents lived in the Númenórean region of Emerië, which she loved dearly.

She was in love with Aldarion for a long while but was reluctant to marry him because of his love of the sea and did not like the time he spent on frequent and long voyages. His commitments to the Guild of Venturers and of their tendency to cut down trees also was of concern to her. They were betrothed in SA 858 and King Meneldur granted her land and built for her a White House in Emerië, as a betrothal gift. They were finally married in SA 870 and had one child in the spring of SA 873, a daughter they named Ancalimë, the future Tar-Ancalimë who was the first of the Ruling Queens of Númenor. It seemed to Erendis that Aldarion was always distant from her, and that she had too little time with him between his voyages. Aldarion often returned late, and eventually this caused Erendis to suffer. Finally, Erendis grew estranged from her husband as a result of this unhappiness with him.

She took her daughter to be raised on her farm in the countryside of Emerië. When Aldarion returned from his latest journey, he decreed that his daughter be returned from her place of dwelling to live with him in Armenelos. Erendis grudgingly did as he commanded, but out of pride she never returned to him, and they were all but divorced in SA 882. In SA 985, when she heard that Tar-Aldarion was returning from his last voyage, she apparently drowned herself in the Bay of Rómenna.
